newsitem.title: SYRIA: Greek foreign minister in talks with Syrians.
newsitem.headline: Greek foreign minister in talks with Syrians.

text.p: Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos held talks in Damascus on Tuesday on ways to advance the Syrian-Israeli peace talks, officials said.
Pangalos told reporters on arrival in the Syrian capital that Greece, as a member of the European Union, wanted to listen to Syrian views on developments of the Middle East peace process.
"Greece and Syria who maintain good ties have used their relations to promote peace and stability in the region," Pangalos said.
He said that Athens wanted a quick resumption of the Syrian-Israeli negotiations, suspended since the election of Benjamin Netanyahu as prime miniser of Israel in May.

Syria has strongly condemned Netanyahu's refusal to trade the occupied Arab lands for peace and refused to resume talks with his government until he agrees to return the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.
Pangalos said that his talks with Syrian leaders would also cover issues related to bilaters economic cooperation and Syria's ties with the EU.
He later met Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara.
